_purpose: Deterministic crosswalk from VEA-1.0's closed-enum vocabulary (doc 01) to verified AAT URIs. Built per doc 06 recommendation (b): VEA never emits AAT IDs itself; this table is applied downstream. Every entry below was resolved via a live fetch against vocab.getty.edu / getty.edu/vow, not from model memory. See doc 06 Appendix / doc 08 Appendix A for the hallucination risk this discipline exists to prevent.

Gelatin silver print.note: Added 2026-09-06 for the Bonhams Group adapter — not yet live-verified against vocab.getty.edu (this project's usual discipline for a new entry), recorded here as an open gap rather than a guessed id. AAT is expected to have a 'gelatin silver print (process)' concept; confirm before relying on this for any AAT-linked query.

Chromogenic print.note: Added 2026-09-06 for the Bonhams Group adapter — same unverified-id caveat as Gelatin silver print above.

Cibachrome print.note: Added 2026-09-06 for the Bonhams Group adapter — same unverified-id caveat as Gelatin silver print above.

Platinum print.note: Added 2026-09-06 for the Bonhams Group adapter — same unverified-id caveat as Gelatin silver print above.

Pigment print.note: Added 2026-09-06 for the Bonhams Group adapter — same unverified-id caveat as Gelatin silver print above. Kept distinct from 'Giclée' above despite likely process overlap, since Bonhams/Skinner's own catalogue text treats 'archival pigment print' as its own term rather than using 'giclée'.

Crayon manner.note: Found missing 2026-09-11 auditing the Navigart public-domain load — two 18th-c Saint-Étienne intaglios read 'Manière de crayon (sanguine) sur papier vergé', one by Demarteau le Jeune who commercialised the process and one inscribed 'gravé . par. Carrée', and both resolved to no technique at all. A roulette-based intaglio process whose entire purpose is imitating a chalk drawing, which is why it reads as a drawing to any medium-string audit. Id verified live against vocab.getty.edu before adding, not guessed; the process-level concept was used (broader term 'intaglio printing processes') rather than the object-type concept 'crayon manner prints' (300041519), matching this crosswalk's own preference for a confirmed process match — see Collotype and Photorelief below. Listed in TECHNIQUE_SUPPRESSES['Intaglio'] because it IS a named intaglio method, so a record naming it should not also collect the umbrella term.

Linocut.note: AAT's PREFERRED label is 'linoleum block printing'; 'linocut (process)' is a registered alternate label under the same concept. Kept as 'Linocut' in VEA's enum to match conventional print-market usage — the URI is what matters for interoperability, not which of AAT's own labels is used.

Screenprint / Serigraphy.note: AAT's confirmed alternate labels include 'screenprinting', 'silk screen printing', 'silk-screen printing'. 'Serigraphy' is standard print-market usage for the same process but was NOT independently confirmed as a registered AAT alternate label in this pass — flagged, not assumed.

Giclée.note: UNMAPPED at process level. Only a PRINT-OBJECT concept exists — 'giclée prints' (300375334) — no separate 'giclée (process)' entry was found in AAT. Record as unmapped per doc 09's discipline rather than force a mapping to the object-level concept.

Collage.note: General image-making technique, distinct from AAT's 'collagraph printing' (300053220) which is a specific printmaking process using collaged materials as the printing plate itself. Met's Medium field uses 'collage' in the general sense (e.g. photographic-print collage elements), so the general concept is the correct match here — but if collagraph printmaking is ever encountered specifically, it should map to 300053220 instead, not this entry.

Chine-collé.note: Moved here from paperSurfaceType — AAT classifies this as a process ('strengthening, stabilizing'), not a paper material, and doc 01 §2C/§2E were updated to match. An additive/compound process, not a standalone technique family: record family: 'mixed' alongside whatever primary technique it was combined with.

Monotype.note: Found missing 2026-09-06 investigating an 11/22-record silent exclusion in a Sidney Nolan BM test pull — 'monotype' was absent from BOTH this crosswalk AND TECHNIQUE_KEYWORDS entirely (not merely unmapped to an aatId), the same has_print_technique()-style silent-exclusion failure mode already documented above for Intaglio/Agathe Sorel, just never triggered before since no prior artist tested (Rembrandt/Trevelyan/Hayter/Sorel) had monotype-technique prints. Verified live against vocab.getty.edu before adding, not guessed.

Collotype.note: Found missing 2026-09-06 investigating 4 records the technique gate (doc 09 §7.13/§7.14) dropped from a Sir Muirhead Bone BM pull — all four literally described 'Collotype reproduction of drawing' (WWI documentary work), 'collotype' absent from both this crosswalk AND TECHNIQUE_KEYWORDS entirely, same silent-exclusion failure mode as Monotype above. A genuine process-level AAT concept was confirmed live (Activities Facet > Processes and Techniques > ... > printing processes > photomechanical processes > planographic photomechanical processes > photolithography), distinct from the separate object-type concept 'collotypes (prints)' (300154355) — the process-level id was used, matching this crosswalk's own preference (see Photorelief below) for a confirmed process match over an object-type-only fallback. Recognizing this only answers 'was a real printmaking process used,' per this project's own established distinction (doc 09 §7.14) — it does not judge whether a given collotype print is a reproduction or an original composition; that's a separate, content-level question this crosswalk was never meant to answer.

Photomechanical print.note: Found missing 2026-09-06 investigating a 14/76-record [EXCLUDED] result in a Richard Hamilton BM pull (10-artist priority-list run) — BM's own structured Technique field says 'photomechanical print' on 7 of his 'artist postcard' records (Object Type still includes 'print'), which extract_techniques() didn't recognize at all, the same has_print_technique()-style silent-exclusion failure mode as Monotype/Intaglio above. UNMAPPED at process level, same discipline as Giclée above: only an object-type concept was confirmed live — 'photomechanical prints' (300041424) — no separate 'photomechanical printing (process)' entry was found distinct from it, so this is recorded as a recognized technique (rescues these records from silent exclusion) without forcing an uncertain process-level aatId. Covered the FIRST of two technique gaps found in the same Hamilton pull; the other — 'digitally generated'/'digital print'/'inkjet'/'dye sublimation print' (7 more excluded records) — is covered by Inkjet print / Dye sublimation print / Digital print below.

Inkjet print.note: Found missing 2026-09-06 in the same Richard Hamilton BM pull that surfaced Photomechanical print above — e.g. Description 'Colour Epson inkjet digital print' on a record whose Object Type still includes 'print'. Unlike Giclée/Photomechanical print, a distinct PROCESS-level AAT concept exists here (Activities facet, broader term 'printing (process)' 300053319) rather than only an object-type 'prints' concept — verified live against vocab.getty.edu, not guessed.

Dye sublimation print.note: AAT's PREFERRED label is 'dye diffusion thermal transfer printing'; 'dye sublimation printing' and 'dye sublimation' are confirmed registered alternate (Used For) labels under the same concept, verified live. A process-level concept (Activities facet, broader term 'printing (process)' 300053319), like Inkjet print above. Found missing 2026-09-06 in the same Richard Hamilton BM pull — e.g. Description 'Digital dye sublimation print'.

Digital print.note: UNMAPPED at process level, same discipline as Giclée/Photomechanical print above: no 'digital printing (process)' entry exists in AAT's Activities facet distinct from Inkjet printing / Dye diffusion thermal transfer printing above. Only an object-type concept was confirmed live — 'digital prints' (300312222) — covering BM's generic Technique values 'digitally generated' and 'digital photographic process' where no more specific inkjet/dye-sublimation process is named. Recorded as a recognized technique (rescues these records from silent exclusion) without forcing an uncertain process-level aatId. Found missing 2026-09-06 in the same Richard Hamilton BM pull as Inkjet print and Dye sublimation print above; suppressed by TECHNIQUE_SUPPRESSES whenever a more specific digital technique also matches.

Stencil printing.note: Found missing 2026-09-06 investigating a 1-record [EXCLUDED] result in a Michael Rothenstein BM pull (10-artist priority-list batch #2) — BM's structured Technique field says 'stencil printing' (Object Type still includes 'print'; the work is a real edition print, 'The love machine', using stencil plus photorelief), which extract_techniques() didn't recognize at all — same has_print_technique()-style silent-exclusion failure mode as Monotype/Photomechanical print above. A distinct PROCESS-level AAT concept exists (Activities Facet, parent 'printing (process)') — verified live against vocab.getty.edu (search 'stencil printing', 3 results, exact term match), not guessed.

Photorelief.note: Found missing in the same Michael Rothenstein BM pull/record as Stencil printing above — BM's Technique field says 'photorelief' (bare, no separate 'photo relief printing' term found under that exact name). Verified live against vocab.getty.edu (search 'photo relief'): no exact-string 'photorelief'/'photo relief printing' concept exists, but 'relief photomechanical processes' (300155634, Activities Facet, scope note 'Photomechanical processes using relief printing surfaces') is a genuine process-level concept matching what BM's own abbreviation denotes — used rather than an object-type-only fallback (the Giclée/Digital print pattern) since a process-level match was actually confirmed, not guessed.

Relief printing.note: Found missing 2026-09-06 investigating a 2/17-record [EXCLUDED] result in a Josef Albers BM pull (10-artist priority-list batch #2) — BM's Technique field says bare 'relief' on two genuine, editioned cork relief-prints ('Inscribed'/'Involute', Danilowitz cat. nos. 114/115, editions of 25), which extract_techniques() didn't recognize at all — same has_print_technique()-style silent-exclusion failure mode as Monotype/Photomechanical print/Stencil printing above. A distinct PROCESS-level AAT concept exists (Activities Facet, direct parent 'printing (process)') — verified live against vocab.getty.edu (search 'relief print', 11 results, exact term match), not guessed. Keyword deliberately kept to the single bare word 'relief' (not 'relief print' or 'relief printing') to match BM's own bare Technique value; TECHNIQUE_SUPPRESSES not needed since no more specific technique in this crosswalk collides with the bare word.

candidates.meaning: modern smooth translucent paper marketed as 'vellum'

vellum.note: Genuinely ambiguous without physical examination — VEA cannot distinguish these from an image alone, and neither should the crosswalk guess. Needs a disambiguation rule (probably: default to parchment for pre-20th-century prints, paper for modern editions) or a VEA-side follow-up question, not a silent pick.

japanese.note: Confirmed unambiguous on lookup — only one matching concept, under Materials > paper (fiber product) > paper by composition or origin.

BFK.note: Not yet verified — BFK Rives is a specific manufacturer's paper brand, likely falls under AAT's Materials facet if present at all; not checked.
